description: Add comprehensive, centralized error handling covering every API endpoint handler in both controllers. Introduce a standard JSON error-response body, a global @RestControllerAdvice that catches specific error types (validation, not-found, conflict, unauthorized/forbidden, and a catch-all), maps each to the appropriate HTTP status, logs each error with request context for debugging, and returns user-friendly messages. Refactor UserController and WalletController to remove their ad-hoc per-method try/catch so all endpoints (POST /user, POST /wallet, PUT /wallet/{id}/money, GET /wallet/{id}, POST /wallet/money-tranfer) route through the global handler. This feature is self-contained; tests are added in FEAT-002.
steps: Create a standard error-response DTO at src/main/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/adapter/rest/dto/ErrorResponseDto.java using the existing Lombok style (@Data @Builder @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor). Fields: java.time.LocalDateTime timestamp, int status, String error, String message, String path. This mirrors the shape referenced by the orchestrator (timestamp, status, error, message, path).

Add message-carrying constructors to the two custom exceptions so handlers/services can supply context, WITHOUT breaking existing callers. In src/main/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/infrastructure/exception/ResourceNotFoundException.java and ResourceExistsException.java: keep the existing public no-arg constructor (existing tests and services call 'new ResourceNotFoundException()' / 'new ResourceExistsException()') and ADD a 'public ResourceNotFoundException(String message){ super(message); }' constructor (same for ResourceExistsException). Do not change that they extend java.lang.Exception.

Create the global handler at src/main/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/infrastructure/exception/GlobalExceptionHandler.java annotated with @org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestControllerAdvice. Use an SLF4J logger (org.slf4j.LoggerFactory.getLogger(GlobalExceptionHandler.class)). Add @ExceptionHandler methods, each accepting the exception plus a jakarta/javax 'javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request' argument to derive the request path (request.getRequestURI()) and method for the log context. Build and return a ResponseEntity<ErrorResponseDto> with the matching status. Mappings: (a) MethodArgumentNotValidException -> HTTP 400 BAD_REQUEST, message aggregating field errors (e.getBindingResult().getFieldErrors() -> 'field: defaultMessage', joined). (b) javax.validation.ConstraintViolationException -> 400 BAD_REQUEST. (c) org.springframework.http.converter.HttpMessageNotReadableException -> 400 BAD_REQUEST (malformed/unreadable JSON body). (d) ResourceNotFoundException -> 404 NOT_FOUND. (e) ResourceExistsException -> 409 CONFLICT. (f) org.springframework.security.access.AccessDeniedException -> 403 FORBIDDEN. (g) org.springframework.security.core.AuthenticationException -> 401 UNAUTHORIZED. (h) a catch-all Exception handler -> 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with a generic user-friendly message (do NOT leak the raw exception message to the client; put the stack/detail only in the log). For each handler: log at WARN for client (4xx) errors and ERROR (with the throwable) for 5xx, always including HTTP method + request URI as context, e.g. log.warn("Resource not found handling {} {}: {}", request.getMethod(), request.getRequestURI(), ex.getMessage()). Client-facing 'message' fields must be user-friendly Spanish or English short phrases (match the project's mixed style; the README is Spanish). Populate ErrorResponseDto.path with request.getRequestURI() and error with the HttpStatus reason phrase.

Refactor src/main/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/adapter/rest/UserController.java: remove the try/catch around createUserService.create(...) and the ResponseStatusException import; let userPost simply return the mapped result and declare 'throws ResourceExistsException' (matching CreateUserService.create's checked signature and the UserWeb interface). The global handler now maps ResourceExistsException -> 409. Keep @Valid on the body.

Refactor src/main/java/es/jguimar/tinybankAPI/adapter/rest/WalletController.java: remove all try/catch blocks and the ResponseStatusException / HttpStatus imports; each method returns the mapped result directly and declares 'throws ResourceNotFoundException' where the underlying WalletService method throws it (moneyToWalletPut, walletGet, moneyTransferPost). walletPost stays as-is (no checked exception). The global handler maps ResourceNotFoundException -> 404. Keep @Valid on bodies.

If the inbound port interfaces (UserWeb.java / WalletWeb.java) need their method signatures to declare the checked exceptions so the @Override compiles, add 'throws ResourceNotFoundException' / 'throws ResourceExistsException' to the corresponding interface methods. Verify the @Override in each controller still matches the interface.

Do NOT edit the generated MapStruct files under src/main/generated/. Do NOT change build.gradle dependencies (slf4j comes transitively via spring-boot-starter; javax.servlet + spring-security are already present).
acceptance_criteria: A GlobalExceptionHandler annotated with @RestControllerAdvice exists and defines @ExceptionHandler methods for validation (MethodArgumentNotValidException -> 400), ResourceNotFoundException (-> 404), ResourceExistsException (-> 409), Spring Security AccessDeniedException (-> 403) and AuthenticationException (-> 401), and a catch-all Exception (-> 500).
Every handler logs the error with request context (at minimum HTTP method and request URI) using an SLF4J logger.

Every handler returns an ErrorResponseDto body containing timestamp, status, error, message and path; the 500 handler returns a generic message and does not echo the raw exception detail to the client.
UserController and WalletController no longer contain per-method try/catch or bare ResponseStatusException usage; all five endpoints rely on the global handler.
The custom exceptions retain their no-arg constructors AND gain a String-message constructor.
All changed and added .java files are syntactically valid Java and reference only types already on the classpath (Spring Web, Spring Security core, javax.validation, javax.servlet, slf4j, Lombok).
verification: Preferred (requires network + JDK 11): from tiny-bank/, run 'JAVA_HOME=/root/.local/share/mise/installs/java/11.0.2 ./gradlew build' and confirm it compiles. This is BLOCKED in the current sandbox (no Gradle distribution, no dependency cache, registries return 403).

Sandbox fallback: syntactically validate each new/changed .java file (e.g. via a Java parser or careful review) and confirm imports resolve to classpath types; confirm UserController/WalletController compile-time obligations (checked-exception declarations match interface + service signatures).
Confirm no references to org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException remain in the two controllers (grep for ResponseStatusException in adapter/rest should return nothing).
findings: Implemented all steps on disk. Added ErrorResponseDto (adapter/rest/dto) with @Data/@Builder/@NoArgsConstructor/@AllArgsConstructor and fields timestamp(LocalDateTime), status(int), error, message, path. Added String-message constructors to ResourceNotFoundException and ResourceExistsException while keeping their existing no-arg constructors (explicitly declared both no-arg and String ctors). Created GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice) in infrastructure/exception with SLF4J logger and @ExceptionHandler methods: MethodArgumentNotValidException->400 (aggregates field errors as 'field: defaultMessage' joined by ', '), ConstraintViolationException->400, HttpMessageNotReadableException->400, ResourceNotFoundException->404, ResourceExistsException->409, Spring Security AccessDeniedException->403, AuthenticationException->401, catch-all Exception->500 (generic Spanish message, logs throwable at ERROR, never leaks raw detail). 4xx logged at WARN, 5xx at ERROR; every handler logs HTTP method + request URI via HttpServletRequest. Each returns ResponseEntity<ErrorResponseDto> with HttpStatus reason phrase as 'error' and request.getRequestURI() as 'path'. Refactored UserController (removed try/catch + ResponseStatusException/HttpStatus imports, userPost now 'throws ResourceExistsException') and WalletController (removed all try/catch + ResponseStatusException/HttpStatus imports; moneyToWalletPut/walletGet/moneyTransferPost declare 'throws ResourceNotFoundException'; walletPost unchanged). Added matching 'throws' clauses to UserWeb.userPost and WalletWeb.moneyToWalletPut/walletGet/moneyTransferPost so @Override matches; walletPost interface method left without throws. Did not touch src/main/generated MapStruct impls or build.gradle. VALIDATION: Real build is BLOCKED in sandbox as documented (no Gradle 6.8.3 distribution: wrapper only has jar/properties; no ~/.gradle/caches, no dependency jars, registries return 403). Validated by careful review: confirmed all imports resolve to types already on the classpath (spring-web: HttpStatus/ResponseEntity/HttpMessageNotReadableException/MethodArgumentNotValidException/ExceptionHandler/RestControllerAdvice; spring-security-core present in build.gradle line 31: AccessDeniedException/AuthenticationException; javax.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest; javax.validation.ConstraintViolationException; org.slf4j; Lombok), removed an unused org.springframework.validation.FieldError import, and confirmed controller checked-exception declarations line up with service signatures (CreateUserService.create throws ResourceExistsException; WalletService.putMoney/showWallet/transferMoney throw ResourceNotFoundException; WalletService.create throws nothing) and the inbound interfaces. grep for ResponseStatusException under adapter/rest returns nothing. Note: 'gradlew' shows as modified in git with 0 content changes (mode-only); not staged as it is unrelated to this feature. Tests are deferred to FEAT-002.
